subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless row, or must OpenClaw provide an ownership migration or repair path before enforcing that rule?
rationale: Foreign-owned mutations clearly violate the existing plugin isolation invariant, but authority over persisted rows created before ownership metadata existed is a security and upgrade-policy choice that cannot be resolved safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject every ownerless row for plugin-runtime callers and retain operator or non-plugin management as the supported recovery path.

options.title: Add ownership migration
options.body: Provide a narrow doctor or migration path for legacy rows whose creating plugin can be established safely before enforcing denial.

options.title: Split legacy policy
options.body: Land foreign-owner denial while moving ownerless-row enforcement into separate maintainer-owned work.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject every ownerless row for plugin-runtime callers and retain operator or non-plugin management as the supported recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history most directly connects Peter to the shared session projection, ownership, and plugin-runtime identity boundaries involved in this policy choice.
